name: WIP limits & gates visible on the board
description: Surface the two protocol vocabularies the UI doesn't render: lane headers show count vs configured WIP limit (loud when over), and epic cards wear a lock chip naming their gate until a human opens it. Advise, don't enforce — no drop is blocked; enforcement stays in the agent protocol (PROTOCOL §3).
notes: Workflow impact: humans watching the live board see the rules agent card-motion obeys — over-limit lanes light up as they fill, and 'why isn't the agent picking this card' is answered by a visible gate chip instead of a trip to config.json. Decomposed from idea-wip-gates-ui (ready to implement, 2026-08-08).

name: Context docs visible in the epic modal
description: Render an epic's context_docs as read-only labeled chips in the edit modal; clicking a chip copies its path for pasting into an editor or another Claude session. Editing stays file/skill-only — the no-widget stance holds for writes.
notes: Workflow impact: with decompose-before-build, every approved idea becomes an epic the human reviews in this modal — the reading list is now visible (and copyable) at exactly that moment instead of living only in JSON. Decomposed from idea-context-docs-chips (ready to implement, 2026-08-08).

name: Ratify review panel — see what changed since last commit
description: A pending-changes badge on the header's saved dot and a review panel listing every uncommitted board change as card-level statements ('B1 moved Backlog → Done', 'idea-x → ready for review', 'epics reordered') — the server diffs the data dir against HEAD semantically. Turns commit-=-ratify into an informed review.
notes: Workflow impact: before saying 'save', the human reviews the pending set in the tool instead of ratifying blind or dropping to the terminal. First server capability that reads git — the endpoint + semantic differ are shared foundation for the briefing and history timeline. Decomposed from idea-ratify-review (top-3 ROI pick #1, user direction 2026-08-08).

name: Ready queue — the 'begin X' menu, visible
description: A strip on the Board page beside Next up listing every pickable story (ready: true, epic unblocked + ungated, unclaimed) grouped by epic, ranked the way the protocol ranks — what a human could hand to an agent right now.
notes: Workflow impact: the human's 'begin X' decision gets a menu — story-grain PROTOCOL §3 made visible, completing what the Next-up strip does for epics. Decomposed from idea-ready-queue (top-3 ROI pick #2, user direction 2026-08-08).

context_docs.label: Board page spec
context_docs.note: Next-up strip — the visual language to match

name: History timeline — the board's git log as a page
description: A #/history page rendering the data dir's commit history as a ratification timeline — date, message, files touched; expanding an entry shows that commit's card-level changes via the ratify differ. Git is already the event store; this is the lens.
notes: Workflow impact: 'when did we decide this' and 'what shipped last week' become clicks; the Board: commit convention becomes visible product, which reinforces it. Third consumer of the git-read capability. Decomposed from idea-history-timeline (top-3 ROI pick #3 — the human had already dragged it to ready to implement).

context_docs.label: Design contract
context_docs.note: new screen → new spec file design/history.md

name: Live refresh moves cards, not pixels
description: When an agent's edit arrives over SSE, changed cards animate: lift (scale + shadow), glide to their new lane/position (FLIP across the re-render), set down. Edited-in-place cards pulse the flash ring; new cards fade in. The board reads like someone physically moving the work.
notes: Workflow impact: watching an agent work now looks like watching a person at a physical board — card motion is the progress narration, no reading required. Direct user request in conversation (2026-08-08), ad hoc → lightweight epic per the decompose-before-build rule.

context_docs.label: System chrome spec
context_docs.note: live refresh — where the motion language lands

name: Story badge: done stories aren't 'ready'
description: Epic cards' story badge counts a story as ready only while it isn't in the done lane — a shipped card reading '2 stories · 2 ready' misstates the queue. Finished ≠ pending, same rule the ready-queue strip already applies.
notes: Direct user request (2026-08-08), spotted on the live board's Done lane.

name: Command palette & quick capture
description: Keyboard-first operation: '/' opens a fuzzy palette over every epic, story, and idea — type, Enter, you're on the card. 'n' captures a new idea from any page. Capture is the funnel's mouth; friction there loses ideas.
notes: Workflow impact: finding a card stops meaning eyeballing lanes; capturing an idea stops meaning navigating to the Ideas page first — one keystroke from anywhere. Decomposed from idea-command-palette (front burner, user go-ahead 2026-08-08).

name: Board briefing — since you last looked
description: A digest when you open the board: what changed since your last visit — card-level statements diffed from your last-seen commit, plus stale claims. The session-break catch-up, computed instead of remembered.
notes: Workflow impact: resuming after time away starts with a computed catch-up instead of mental diffing or reading git log. Third consumer of the git-read capability. Decomposed from idea-board-briefing (front burner, user go-ahead 2026-08-08).

name: ./board stop — kill a running board from the CLI
description: The port-busy error now says how to stop the squatter, and a ./board stop [port] subcommand does it: shows what's listening, kills it. No more hunting for lsof incantations.
notes: Direct user request (2026-08-08) after hitting EADDRINUSE against a board another session had started.

name: Chrome fixes: briefing hidden override, rows-mode top leak
description: Two rendering bugs: (1) .briefing{display:flex} defeats the hidden attribute, so an empty banner ('view dismiss' with no text) shows on boards where it should be hidden; (2) in rows mode, scrolled swimlane content shows through the board container's top padding band above the sticky lane strip.
notes: Direct user report with screenshot (2026-08-08, arc board). Both are implementation bugs — the specs already describe the correct behavior; no spec change.

name: Story states with personality
description: One storyState() rule for every surface, with fun labels: middle-lane stories show their activity by kind (cooking / testing / tidying up / writing / wiring up), done stories say '✓ shipped / plated / in the books' — or '✓ done · waiting on A2-4' while siblings lag — and blocked-but-ready stories name their blocker. Kills the last '✓ ready in Done' surface (rows cards).
notes: Direct user request with screenshot (2026-08-08): review status logic end to end, expand 'Cooking'-style descriptions. Workflow impact: the rows board reads as a narrated kitchen — what's being done to each story and who/what it waits on, at a glance.

name: Ship & archive — completed epics leave the board
description: An epic whose stories are all done can be closed: archived_at stamps it, and it moves off the active board into a Shipped view (Current/Shipped toggle beside Epics|Rows — the Ideas page's archive pattern). Done-column items stay put until the whole epic closes; archived epics still count for milestones and dependencies.
notes: Direct user request (2026-08-08): remove complete epics from the board, keep them reachable (toggle over history page — chosen for consistency with the ideas archive), leave stories in Done until the epic closes, then clean up the board. Workflow impact: the active board only ever shows live work; shipped work becomes a browsable museum.

name: Agent onboarding — the contract explains itself on arrival
description: An agent should be able to act correctly within one short read. AGENTS.md gains a §0 orientation map (what this is, the five files, the five surfaces, the inviolable rules, where depth lives); the skill lists what the tool can do today; PROTOCOL learns about archived_at; CAPABILITIES and README catch up with the twelve features shipped this session; and the contract itself becomes fetchable over HTTP so an agent with only the URL can read it.
notes: Workflow impact: onboarding drops from ~600 lines of prose to a ~40-line map that names everything and points at depth on demand. Direct user request (2026-08-08). Audit found real drift: archived_at absent from PROTOCOL, './board stop' documented nowhere, SKILL.md unaware of every feature shipped today.

name: Dependency status you can see at a glance
description: Each dependency on a card becomes its own chip colored by whether it's satisfied — cleared deps go green with a ✓, outstanding ones stay loud. When the last one clears and nothing else blocks the card, the card itself turns: a green edge, a faint wash, and a '▶ ready to start' marker. The moment work becomes available is visible without reading anything.
notes: Workflow impact: 'what unblocked while I was away' becomes ambient — a dep clearing repaints its chip, and the final one repaints the whole card, animated by the live-refresh FLIP. Direct user request (2026-08-09).

name: Deterministic visual language for the ideas board
description: Color stops competing with itself: one meaning per hue, carried by a left border and a matching status pill instead of heavy card tints. Cards answer five questions in five seconds — what is it, why does it matter, what does it unlock, how hard is it, what's stopping us — with the prose moved to the deep dive. New fields make the reasoning explicit: why now, the decision a reviewer must make, and conviction as a dimension separate from workflow state.
notes: Workflow impact: the ideas board becomes a product-reasoning surface rather than a wall of prose — you sit down with it to resolve named decisions, and dependency leverage (what an idea unlocks) is visible so foundational work stops looking like an isolated feature. From the user's design critique (2026-08-09); the green 'clear to pursue' shipped in B15 is one of the ambiguities being corrected.

name: Ideas as a funnel: maturity signal, progressive cards, promotion boundary
description: Model the ideas page as what it actually is — a funnel deciding what deserves to enter execution — rather than a second Kanban. Colour becomes a maturity scale (gray dormant → blue shaping → amber decide → green cleared) with nothing else on the card allowed to compete. Cards grow as they mature: a back-burner card is a title and a bet; a review card leads with its decision; a ready card states outcome, constraints and acceptance. A 'Promote to Board' action makes the graduation from discovery to delivery an explicit, recorded moment.
notes: Workflow impact: Ideas answers 'what might this become', the Board answers 'what are we building', and Promote is the boundary between them — the decompose-before-build rule becomes a button instead of a convention. From the user's funnel reframing (2026-08-09), refining B16.

name: Execution board reoriented around agent work
description: The board should answer what an agent can start now, what is running, what needs a human, and what is blocked. Today its chrome and its completed work crowd out the two epics actually in flight. Collapse what is memory (back burner, done work), condense the filter wall, give agents a way to say 'I need you' distinctly from 'I am blocked', restructure lanes to Ready | In Progress | Review | Done, and close the loop by showing an idea what shipped from it.
notes: Workflow impact: Ideas and Board stop being two boards and become one product-development system with a visible boundary — promote in, provenance back. Review becomes a first-class state because an agent finishing code is not the work being done. From the user's execution-board critique (2026-08-09).

name: One work queue, one source of truth
description: Next up (epic-grain) and Ready to pick up (story-grain) answered the same question differently, so the board could say 'nothing pickable' directly above three ready stories. Merge them into a single work queue that reports the most actionable state: what an agent can start, what is in flight and who owns it, or why nothing is available.
notes: Workflow impact: the board has one answer to 'what now', and claimed work shows its owner — the first step toward the board being an orchestration surface rather than a report. From the user's execution critique (2026-08-09).

name: Idea deep dive: fill the page, edit in place
description: Prose was capped at ~72 characters inside a 1000px column, leaving a ragged void down the left side, and the long-form fields could only be edited through the cramped 'Edit core' modal. Let the columns carry their content, and make every prose region on the page editable where it sits.
notes: Workflow impact: the deep dive becomes a document you write in rather than a read-only view with a modal bolted on. Edit core shrinks to what it is good at — small structured metadata. Direct user request with screenshot (2026-08-09).

name: Claim hygiene — sessions end, claims don't
description: A claimed card whose agent walked away looks like work in flight forever, and PROTOCOL §3 treats 'already claimed' as a reason a card is unpickable — so a dead claim silently removes real work from the queue. Show how long every claim has been held, mark the ones old enough to be suspect, and let a human release one in a single action.
notes:
Workflow impact: the selection rule stops quietly shrinking as sessions end. Promoted from idea-claim-hygiene (2026-08-10) on the user's go-ahead.

Why now: this session alone stranded claims on two boards. Constraints: no new fields — reuse claimed_at and the briefing's staleness computation; never auto-clear a claim, since a long job and an abandoned one look identical from outside. Open decision the human still owns: whether 48h is the right threshold.

name: Milestone progress you can see
description: One aggregate bar per milestone answering 'how far along is this overall', plus a mini-bar per deliverable so the laggard is obvious. The page already computes done/total per deliverable; it just never draws it.
notes:
Workflow impact: 'where are we on M1' is answered by looking rather than by arithmetic across deliverable chips.

Decision resolved from precedent (see the idea's log): counts EPICS, and archived epics still count — archiving hides, never deletes. Promoted from idea-milestone-burnup (2026-08-10).

name: Board data survives what the UI writes
description:
A save through the board UI mangled an em-dash in an arc card into replacement characters, and nothing said so. Request bodies were accumulated with `data += chunk`, which decodes every chunk on its own, so a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence landing across a chunk boundary is destroyed on both sides of the split. Which character breaks is a function of where the boundary falls, not of what the text says — three other em-dashes in the same field came through intact, which is exactly why it went unnoticed.

These backlogs are prose. Em-dashes, accented names, arrows and quotes are everywhere in them, every save goes through this path, and the damage is silent and cumulative.
notes:
Workflow impact: none visible — which is the point. The fault only ever showed up as text quietly going wrong days later, in a card nobody was looking at.

Fixed by collecting Buffers and decoding once at the end, which also makes the 5 MB cap count bytes rather than UTF-16 code units. A write-time warning backs it up: U+FFFD is what a broken decode leaves behind and no card should ever legitimately hold one, so its presence means text was mangled upstream. It warns rather than refuses — losing an author's edit is worse than keeping a damaged character, and the warning is what makes the damage findable instead of silent.
